brief: GS's Garrett frames 2026 as a year of two halves. H1 produced broad gains across equities, sectors and momentum (NDX Sharpe at a post-1990s high in June), while H2 compressed conviction horizons from six months to days, leaving clients without a directional view into year end. Against that, GS lays out its 2027 outlook. Hatzius forecasts 2.8% global growth on lower energy prices and strong capex, flagging Iran escalation, fiscal deficits and weaker AI spending as downside risks. Wilson sees a maturing cycle with the AI impulse peaking and bonds regaining hedging value. Oppenheimer stays bullish, overweight US and Japan, underweight Europe. Triveda sees the dollar firming near term then softening through 2027 as the yen gains policy support. Rindels sees AI capex reaching $1.4tn by end-2027, about 4% of US GDP. Separately, options markets are convinced November 5th's selloff was isolated, with year-end SPX and NDX straddles now pricing below that session's move. Flow desks show hedge funds still de-risking, with equities sold 5 of the last 6 weeks, tech exposure at decade lows and NVDA supply rotating into other megacap names, while retail participation holds up. Momentum positioning has unwound as AI names fill momentum's short leg.
